benchmarkComparisons: unmeasured: inventory is a census, not a benchmark
knownLimitations: capability to test mapping is curated; a capability is VERIFIED only for the tests mapped to it, not for every behaviour it has
5 documents state 17 MCP tools while the server registers 23: recorded as a mismatch, corrected under E8-04

benchmarkComparisons: baseline gates (clean worktree of the measured commit, all valid): cve-replay, mutation, protection-verdict, layer-recall, provenance-accuracy, self-scan and independent-gate all passed; they are regression checks, not accuracy; independent accuracy: unmeasured until E1-04
knownLimitations: gate pass means the existing gate exits 0; the curated regression net is at its ceiling by construction
a second git worktree needs the gitignored vendored java parser (see DECISIONS D8)

benchmarkComparisons: unmeasured: a contract snapshot, not a benchmark
knownLimitations: the snapshot records shapes and closed vocabularies, not values; a behavioural change that keeps the shape is not caught here
exit codes are captured on two small fixtures only
scan state written into a scanned directory changes the next scan's JSON shape (sbomDiff.first), so captures scan fresh copies

benchmarkComparisons: unmeasured: E0-04 is tooling, no benchmark applies
knownLimitations: dependency edges are hand-written from epic-level statements in the PRD (see DECISIONS.md)

benchmarkComparisons: unmeasured: E0-05 is tooling, no benchmark applies
knownLimitations: the Windows process-tree termination path is the shared supervisor's and is not exercised on this macOS host
evidence logs are machine-local (gitignored); a fresh clone must run task.mjs reverify to re-establish them

benchmarkComparisons: unmeasured: example counts come from an archived run of engine 0.137.1 and say where to look first, not how accurate anything is
knownLimitations: impact per CWE class is a fixed table; effort sizes are estimates

benchmarkComparisons: unmeasured: provenance audit of 1004 entries in 424 repositories: licences read for all 424 repositories (82 assert none), 34 sampled entries confirmed against the upstream host, 0 missing; acquisition checksums are empty until entries are fetched (E1-04)
knownLimitations: reconstructable means the manifest names repository, both commits and advisory; only a sample of 34 entries was confirmed upstream
the licence lookup and upstream check are opt-in network steps

benchmarkComparisons: split leakage: the older per-id held-out slice has 91 of 424 repositories on both sides (533 of 1004 entries); the new grouped split has 0 straddling groups; splits dev 591, validation 204, sealed 209 over 423 groups
knownLimitations: no time dimension: the manifest has no advisory publication date
kotlin and csharp have too few sealed entries for a rate (insufficient_population)

benchmarkComparisons: the scorer reproduces the archived runner result exactly on real data (localized, file and wide counts) and reconciles every denominator; no new accuracy figure is claimed
knownLimitations: grouped-bootstrap intervals need at least 10 independent groups, otherwise they are unmeasured
the minimum for a rate (30 scored entries) is a declared planning value

benchmarkComparisons: mutation gate (npm run bench:mutation:check): verdict flip 217/217 (metamorphic 28/28, adversarial 35/35, label-invariance 154/154), 5 known gaps held (3 false positives, 2 false negatives); the gate takes about 11 seconds
knownLimitations: the new cases were written by the same party as the detectors, from documentation idioms rather than detector rules; 6 of 48 share one idiomatic line with the regression corpus

the 5 known gaps are real engine limitations found by this work (constant concatenation and list-membership SQL, Ruby where(id: ...), fs.readFileSync traversal, Spring JdbcTemplate) and are not fixed here

benchmarkComparisons: unmeasured: an inventory of 16 routes and 10 divergences found by reading the code and confirmed with call tests; 3 divergences were reproduced by running the routes (deny-all and empty patches verified, tests run before the patch yet reported fully verified, apply and verify shapes differ)
knownLimitations: a read-only audit by a second agent produced the route table; the structural test checks that each entry point exists, not that the table is exhaustive
R5, R6, R11, R12, R13 are covered by existing tests, not by new call tests here

benchmarkComparisons: unmeasured: schema and one adapter (verifyFix) built and tested; adapters for the other routes land with E3-03
knownLimitations: only the verifyFix adapter exists; no route emits the record yet (E3-03)

benchmarkComparisons: unmeasured: behavioural change only; 336 existing fix/MCP tests still pass
knownLimitations: autopilot, proof-fabric fix, SCA upgrade and Haskell/Nix routes are not yet routed through verifyPatch (E3-04/E3-06/E3-07)
tests still run on the pre-patch tree; surfaced as degraded, fixed in E3-05
verifiedFull on existing results now follows the canonical record, so it is false where the old value was true but the tests ran pre-patch

benchmarkComparisons: unmeasured: one JavaScript command-injection fixture executed for real in the confined runner (original: exploit fired 2/2; real fix: 0/2; scanner-hiding fake fix: still fires)
knownLimitations: replay needs a reproducer; only JavaScript was run for real here, other languages depend on the host toolchain
local confinement is the lower-assurance userspace sandbox; the container runner is not enabled
execution-proven says the exploit stopped, not that behaviour survived (E3-05)

benchmarkComparisons: unmeasured: behaviour tests on 10 hand-written cases; 503 existing fix, MCP, autopilot and proof-fabric tests still pass
knownLimitations: the footprint check is a text heuristic over operation kinds, not an equivalence proof; it misses subtler behaviour changes and says unobservable when it sees no sensitive operation
authorized-use and unauthorized-use test generation is not built; the check relies on the project's own tests
performance regression and response/schema change detection are not implemented
the IDOR and SQL cases are checked at footprint level; end-to-end through the scanner only the command-injection fixture was run

benchmarkComparisons: unmeasured: policy matrix of 5 tiers x 2 modes plus severity, category and residual-risk cases; existing fix suites still pass
knownLimitations: automatic mode is only enforced where a caller passes applyMode:automatic; nothing in the CLI or MCP sets it today, so default behaviour for requested writes is unchanged
autopilot has no production caller, so policy is not wired into it
the policy is not configurable from a project file yet; it is a function argument
